extracted.intended_audience: PD/PIs, signing officials, research administrators, and other recipients preparing and submitting NIH/AHRQ/VA Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) via eRA Commons
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step instructions and substantive content requirements for preparing, validating, routing, and submitting Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) in eRA Commons for NIH, AHRQ, and VA awards, including special RPPR variants (Final, Interim, Multi-Project, SBIR/STTR, Training, Fellowship, Education).

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR mandatory format and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR is required for all annual non-competing (Type 5) NIH awards and final progress reports (Final-RPPR), including SBIR/STTR awards. NIH requires an Interim-RPPR if a renewal application (Type 2) is submitted on or before the date a Final-RPPR would be required. Annual, interim, and final progress reports submitted in any format other than the RPPR will not be processed by the NIH and will require resubmission through the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to listed NOT-OD notices for more information. AHRQ and VA have agency-specific usage nuances (AHRQ must use eRA RPPR module; VA has reporting differences and outcomes are not published).

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR due dates (NIH SNAP, Non-SNAP, Fellowships, MYF, Final/Interim)
rubrics_metrics.description: SNAP awards: progress report due the 15th of the month preceding the month the budget period ends (extended to next business day if holiday/weekend). Non-SNAP awards: due the first of the month preceding the month the budget period ends. Fellowships: due two months before the next budget period start date. MYF awards: due annually on or before the anniversary of the budget/project period start date. Final and Interim RPPRs: due within 120 days of the end of the period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of Award (NoA) may supersede these dates. Interim-RPPR is required only when a renewal application was submitted on or before the Final-RPPR due date; if the Type 2 is not funded the Interim becomes the Final.

rubrics_metrics.name: AHRQ RPPR specific due date and SNAP participation
rubrics_metrics.description: All AHRQ RPPRs are due 3 months before the anniversary of the award. AHRQ does not participate in SNAP and requires detailed budgets for the parent organization and each consortium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If due date falls on weekend/holiday it extends to next business day. Use AHRQ online help and Closeout instructions for AHRQ-specific closeout actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate and edit the RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the PD/PI or the PD/PI delegate may initiate an RPPR. For multiple PIs (MPI), only the Contact PI or the Contact PI's PD/PI delegate may initiate. Signing Officials (SO) and Administrative Officials (AO) can view and perform organization actions such as submit and certify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To initiate, access via Status or the RPPR module in eRA Commons. Users may work on sections in any order but must click Save before leaving a screen to retain data. For multi-year awards, cannot initiate a year until previous year's RPPR is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR navigation and required sections (A–I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR in eRA Commons consists of separate screens/sections: A Cover Page; B Accomplishments; C Products; D Participants; E Impact; F Changes; G Special Reporting Requirements; H Budget; I Outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can navigate between sections; the system generates a PDF upon submission which is viewable from the RPPR Menu and from Status after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text entry character limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Most text entry boxes have an 8,000 character limit (~3 pages); entry of more than 8,000 characters is prevented by the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH has recommended lengths for some questions and agency-specific text box limits may be less than 8,000. Warning: text exceeding 8,000 characters is cut to 8,000 when using cut-and-paste.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF attachment size and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF file uploads have no page limits but must be no more than 6 megabytes (6MB). Unless otherwise stated, PDFs uploaded to RPPR are required to be flattened PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common Forms (Biosketch, Current & Pending/Other Support) generally should NOT be flattened to retain SciENcv signature validations. Avoid bundling/portfolio PDFs and paginated PDFs; all PDF attachments must be submitted as individual files. Save filenames ≤50 characters, using only A–Z, a–z, 0–9, and underscore (_); do not use special characters or spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include PII or PHI
rubrics_metrics.description: Do Not Include Personal Identifiable Information (PII) Or Protected Health Information (PHI) In the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensitive PII (e.g., SSN, personal financial information, Alien Registration Number) and PHI (e.g., personal medical conditions) must not be included. For NIH grants, additional FAQs and IC Privacy Coordinators are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF file appearance and page layout requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard paper size (8½" x 11"). Use at least one-half inch margins (top, bottom, left, and right) for all pages. No information should appear in the margins, including PD/PI name and page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Arial, Helvetica, Palatino Linotype, or Georgia typeface; black font color; font size 11 points or larger. Type density must be no more than 15 characters per inch and no more than six lines per inch. Symbol fonts may be used for Greek/special characters but maintain font size requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style guidance for RPPR text
rubrics_metrics.description: Use English and avoid jargon. Abbreviations and language that may not be known to the broader scientific community should be avoided unless clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internet URLs should not be used unless specified. Be concise; NIH recommends concise responses and discourages unnecessary detail even in attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving, editing, and system PDF generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must click the Save button in the navigation bar before leaving a screen to retain data entered. Upon submission to the awarding agency, the system will generate a PDF of the progress report viewable from the RPPR Menu or Status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not close the browser or use the browser back button during RPPR tasks; external links open new windows which must be closed to return to the RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for errors and warnings before routing/submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR includes system options to 'Check for Errors' and will display errors and warnings for single-project and multi-project RPPRs; errors must be resolved prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are separate checks for single-project and multi-project RPPRs and examples of common error messages are provided in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing, recall, and submission workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPRs can be routed to reviewers, recalled, and submitted to the awarding agency from the RPPR Menu. Only authorized users (e.g., SOs for certification) can perform certain actions like final submission and certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screenshots and stepwise instructions are provided for routing to next reviewer, recalling the RPPR, submission success messages, and submission errors/warnings (including multi-project submission errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: SO/PD-PI certification upon submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of the RPPR includes a certification: the SO (or PD/PI with delegated authority) certifies that the awardee organization is in compliance with the NoA terms and Awards Policy Statement, and verifies the accuracy and validity of administrative, fiscal, and scientific information in the progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification warns that deliberate withholding, falsification, or misrepresentation could result in withdrawal of the report, suspension/termination, debarment, criminal penalties, and possible reimbursement liability. If unable to certify compliance with assurances/certifications/policies, provide an explanation and upload it in G.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B — Accomplishments: B.1 Major goals and B.2 Accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: B.1: State the major goals of the project. B.2: Describe what was accomplished under these goals for the reporting period, including 1) major activities; 2) significant results, including major findings, developments, or conclusions (positive and negative); and 3) key outcomes or other achievements. Include discussion of stated goals not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-project awards emphasize synergy, collaboration, and integration at the overall level; report component-specific major goals and accomplishments under each component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B — B.3 & B.4 Training and professional development details
rubrics_metrics.description: B.3: Brief description of significant activities and major lessons learned. B.4: Describe what opportunities for training and professional development the project provided (training = advanced professional skills transfer; professional development = workshops, conferences, seminars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For programs involving participants include relevant program statistics (e.g., doctoral training Table 8A for D43/U2R). For Education awards note specific applicability and exceptions in chapter 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section C — Products (C.1–C.5) and Data Management and Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: C.1–C.5 capture products resulting from the project including publications, intellectual property, research tools, other products, resource sharing, and Data Management and Sharing (C.5.c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.5.c: incorporate progress reporting requirements for the Data Management and Sharing Plan where applicable (policy applicability depends on NIH activity code and application submission date). For multi-project awards, DMS may be reported at the overall component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section D — Participants, Senior/Key Personnel, Level of Effort, and Other Support
rubrics_metrics.description: D.1: Identify Senior/Key Personnel and other participants and provide contact and affiliation details. D.2: Provide personnel updates such as level of effort (D.2.a) and MPI Leadership Plan changes (D.2.e). Include uploads for new Senior/Key Personnel and changes in Current & Pending and Other Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-component awards specify component(s) on which an individual worked. Use Ctrl to select multiple components when assigning personnel to components. Follow new Common Form Biosketch and Current & Pending (Other) Support adoption guidance where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section E — Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: E.1–E.4 request descriptions of impact. For example, E.1 asks what is the impact on the development of human resources (describe changes in opportunities, skills, retention, dissemination of materials, exposure to science and technology), and for multi-component awards component-level E.3 asks impact on technology transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report measurable or demonstrable impacts and examples such as transfer to government/industry, start-up formation, or adoption of new practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section F — Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: F.1 Describe changes in approach and reasons for change, including role of external advisory committees and how changes strengthen objectives. F.3 Report significant changes to Human Subjects, Vertebrate Animals, Biohazards, and/or Select Agents with descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes relate to a specific component in multi-project awards, report under that component. Provide PDF attachments when substantial protocol or protection changes require documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section G — Special Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: G.1–G.12 capture special reporting items: human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, select agents, SBIR/STTR foreign disclosure questions, disclosures of foreign affiliations/relationships to foreign countries, Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment certification, and other sponsor/NoA/NOFO-specific reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some items are award-type specific (e.g., SBIR/STTR foreign disclosure appears only for SBIR/STTR awards). Refer to NOA/NOFO for award-specific reporting obligations. For VA/AHRQ there are agency-specific instructions in their links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section H — Budget instructions (non-SNAP and SNAP distinctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section H applies to non-SNAP awards (detailed SF 424 R&R or PHS 398 budget forms). For multi-project and subaward/consortium budgets, recipients may select up to 30 subaward budgets. SNAP awards have different F&A applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Single-Project RPPRs with Complicated Structure follow competing application budget instructions; upload budget justification as item L and include detailed justification for significant changes (e.g., total re-budgeting >25% of total award amount). If subaward budgets are completed system may not calculate F.5 for main budget; manually compute total consortium costs and enter into F.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Project RPPR overall vs component reporting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project RPPRs certain items are reported at the overall level (e.g., emphasis on synergy in B.1, overall accomplishments in B.2 with component-specific reporting under each component) while other items like some DMS activities are reported at the overall component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow component instructions (7.6.2) for adding components and completing component-level A–I with specified exceptions (many fields Not Applicable at component level). Budgets: complete project and subaward budgets for each component; a system-generated summary budget consolidates component budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component assignment for personnel in multi-project RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding Senior/Key Personnel or Other Significant Contributors for a multi-component award, specify the component(s) on which the individual worked by editing the participant record and selecting one or more components (use Ctrl to select multiple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This personnel information is for the entire project and must be accurate to reflect effort across components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access and Additional Materials (PRAM, FRAM, IRAM, Agency-Requested PRAM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR module includes functionality and instructions for Public Access Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM), Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM), Interim Report Additional Materials (IRAM), and Agency-Requested PRAMs including initiation, recall, submission, and viewing for multi-year funded awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate workflows exist for initiating, routing, certifying, recalling, and viewing each PRAM/FRAM/IRAM type; SO certification may be required for public access PRAM submission. Follow chapter 5 subsections for stepwise actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flattened vs non-flattened PDFs and SciENcv forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stated, PDF files uploaded to RPPR are required to be flattened PDFs; however, Common Forms (Biosketch and Current & Pending/Other Support) in most cases should NOT be flattened to retain SciENcv signature validations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful to preserve signature validations when required; flattened PDFs remove layers/forms and signatures and may invalidate embedded validations.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Save all files with descriptive file names of 50 characters or less and use only standard characters: A–Z, a–z, 0–9, and underscore (_).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use special characters (e.g., &, -, *, %, /, #) or spaces. Use underscores for word separation (e.g., My_Attached_File.pdf). File names are displayed in the assembled PDF submitted to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education, Training, Fellowship, K, SBIR/STTR RPPR exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific RPPR types (Individual Career Development K; Fellowships; SBIR/STTR; Training; Education) have tailored instructions and exceptions to the standard A–I instructions, such as different applicability of C.3/C.4/C.5, requirements for program statistics (Table 8A), responsible conduct of research reporting, and SBIR/STTR foreign disclosure form appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to chapter 7 for full supplemental instructions per RPPR type. For example: Education awards have special B.4 training guidance; K awards and Training awards have special NOA/NOFO reporting requirements; SBIR/STTR RPPRs include foreign disclosure forms and required reporting of foreign affiliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act and government use of RPPR information
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH maintains application and grant records as part of systems of records as defined by the Privacy Act (NIH 09-25-0036 and related).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government use of information is governed by the Privacy Act statement; users should be aware of the records systems referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances, Certifications, and inability to certify
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of Assurances and Certifications and other policies applicants/recipients must comply with are referenced in the NIH Grants Policy Statement or HHS Grants Policy Statement as applicable. If unable to certify compliance, provide an explanation and upload it in G.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission includes a certification by the SO (or PD/PI with delegated authority) confirming compliance and accountability for appropriate use of funds and accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and line-density requirements for attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specified fonts and sizes; type density no more than 15 characters per inch and no more than six lines per inch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures readability and system compatibility. Symbol fonts allowed for special characters provided size rules are still met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling re-budgeting and significant budget changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget justification (item L) must include detailed justification for line items and amounts that represent a significant change from previously recommended levels (example: total re-budgeting greater than 25 percent of the total award amount for this budget period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single-project complicated-structure RPPRs and multi-project components, provide detailed justifications; if subaward budgets are provided the system may not compute certain summary fields requiring manual entry (e.g., F.5 consortium totals).
